Get a user's access token for another R package

Source: R/session.R
oauth_db_token.Rd

Use this when an R function accepts an access token directly. Call the returned function for a current token each time you make a request.

Usage

oauth_db_token(
  authorization,
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

auth$connection from a shinyOAuth server module, without parentheses. To select a saved authorization, pass a function that calls auth$connection(id).

target

Token target name in the shinyOAuth client. NULL uses its default token, including for clients without named targets.

required_scopes

Additional permissions to check before use. Request consent and set the client's permission requirements in shinyOAuth.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

session

Shiny session. Inferred when the helper is created in server().

Value

A reactive function returning a bearer token string. Call bearer() inside the user's Shiny session.

Details

For Fabric or Databricks functions, the platform API clients below can supply the credentials for you.

shinyOAuth obtains or renews the token. Keep the function in the Shiny session and get a token for each operation; a copied token string keeps its own expiry time.

See also

oauth_db_fabric_api(), oauth_db_databricks_api(). See vignette("getting-started", package = "shinyOAuthDB") for token lifetime.

Other advanced connection helpers: oauth_db_connect(), oauth_db_fabric()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
bearer <- oauth_db_token(auth$connection, required_scopes = "all-apis")
output$rows <- shiny::renderPrint({
  brickster::db_sql_warehouse_list(
    host = "example.cloud.databricks.com",
    token = bearer()
  )
})
} # }
